André de Foix, Seigneur de Lesparre, (1490–1547) was a French General.

Born into a noble family, de Foix began his military career in the French army at a young age, quickly rising through the ranks due to his exceptional bravery and strategic thinking.

In 1522, de Foix led the French forces to a decisive victory at the Battle of Pavia, which marked a significant turning point in the Italian Wars and cemented his reputation as a brilliant military commander.

De Foix's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the French Renaissance.

As he lay dying in 1547, de Foix reflected on his life and the many battles he had fought, saying "Je suis mort pour ma patrie, et je suis mort pour mon honneur" – 'I died for my country, and I died for my honor'.

Despite his passing, de Foix's influence can still be felt in modern-day France, where he remains a celebrated figure in military history and a symbol of French patriotism.

André de Foix, Seigneur de Lesparre (1490–1547) was a French General who played a significant role in the medieval era, specifically during the Italian Wars.

Born in Foix, France, de Foix was a member of the powerful House of Foix, which had strong ties to the French monarchy. His military campaigns were marked by his bravery and strategic thinking, which earned him recognition from his contemporaries and historians alike.

De Foix's military successes included the Battle of Pavia in 1525, where he fought alongside Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, and the Battle of Ravenna in 1521, where he led French troops to victory against the Italian condottieri.

De Foix's legacy can be seen in the modern-day French military, which continues to draw inspiration from his campaigns and tactics. His influence can also be seen in the development of modern artillery and siege warfare.

Despite his significant contributions to the French military, de Foix's life was cut short in 1547, when he was wounded in battle at the Siege of Saint-Gaudens. He died soon after, and was buried in the Lesparre family tomb in the Lesparre church.

In conclusion, André de Foix was a remarkable figure in medieval European history, whose bravery, strategic thinking, and military successes had a lasting impact on the development of modern warfare.
